1	// Package codec implements encoding and decoding of single binary frames
2	// in a length-prefixed wire format.
3	//
4	// Wire layout (all multi-byte fields big-endian):
5	//
6	//	+------------+---------+--------+------+----------+=========+
7	//	| length (4) | ver (1) | flags(2)| kind(1)| cksum(2) | payload |
8	//	+------------+---------+--------+------+----------+=========+
9	//
10	// The 4-byte length counts payload bytes only. The 10-byte header is
11	// length + version + flags + kind + checksum. The checksum is the low
12	// 16 bits of the byte-wise sum of all header bytes except the checksum
13	// field itself, plus every payload byte.
14	package codec
15	
16	import (
17		"encoding/binary"
18		"errors"
19	)
20	
21	const (
22		// Version is the only protocol version this codec reads and writes.
23		Version = 1
24	
25		// HeaderSize is the total header length in bytes:
26		// 4 (length) + 1 (version) + 2 (flags) + 1 (kind) + 2 (checksum).
27		HeaderSize = 10
28	
29		// MaxPayload is the maximum payload size in bytes a frame may carry.
30		MaxPayload = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB
31	)
32	
33	var (
34		// ErrShortFrame is returned when the input is too short to contain a
35		// complete frame.
36		ErrShortFrame = errors.New("codec: short frame")
37		// ErrBadVersion is returned when the frame version is not supported.
38		ErrBadVersion = errors.New("codec: unsupported version")
39		// ErrChecksum is returned when the checksum does not match the
40		// recomputed value.
41		ErrChecksum = errors.New("codec: checksum mismatch")
42		// ErrTooLarge is returned when the payload exceeds MaxPayload.
43		ErrTooLarge = errors.New("codec: payload too large")
44	)
45	
46	// Frame is a single decoded frame, or the input to Encode.
47	type Frame struct {
48		Version uint8
49		Flags   uint16
50		Kind    uint8
51		Payload []byte
52	}
53	
54	// checksum sums every byte of header-and-payload except the checksum
55	// field itself and keeps the low 16 bits.
56	func checksum(data []byte) uint16 {
57		var sum uint32
58		for _, b := range data {
59			sum += uint32(b)
60		}
61		return uint16(sum)
62	}
63	
64	// Encode serializes f into the wire format. The version written is
65	// always Version. It returns ErrTooLarge if the payload exceeds
66	// MaxPayload.
67	func Encode(f Frame) ([]byte, error) {
68		if len(f.Payload) > MaxPayload {
69			return nil, ErrTooLarge
70		}
71	
72		out := make([]byte, HeaderSize+len(f.Payload))
73		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[0:4], uint32(len(f.Payload)))
74		out[4] = Version
75		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[5:7], f.Flags)
76		out[7] = f.Kind
77		copy(out[HeaderSize:], f.Payload)
78	
79		// Sum the header bytes before the checksum field plus the payload.
80		sum := checksum(out[0:8]) + checksum(out[HeaderSize:])
81		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[8:10], sum)
82		return out, nil
83	}
84	
85	// Decode parses one frame from data. On any error it returns the zero
86	// Frame and one of ErrShortFrame, ErrBadVersion, ErrChecksum or
87	// ErrTooLarge; checks run in that order so the same corrupt input always
88	// yields the same error.
89	func Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error) {
90		var f Frame
91	
92		// 1. Length: enough bytes for the header, then for the declared payload.
93		if len(data) < HeaderSize {
94			return f, ErrShortFrame
95		}
96		payloadLen := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[0:4])
97		if uint64(len(data)) < uint64(HeaderSize)+uint64(payloadLen) {
98			return f, ErrShortFrame
99		}
100	
101		// 2. Version.
102		version := data[4]
103		if version != Version {
104			return f, ErrBadVersion
105		}
106	
107		// 3. Checksum over header (minus the checksum field) and payload.
108		want := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[8:10])
109		got := checksum(data[0:8]) + checksum(data[HeaderSize:HeaderSize+int(payloadLen)])
110		if got != want {
111			return f, ErrChecksum
112		}
113	
114		// 4. Size.
115		if payloadLen > MaxPayload {
116			return f, ErrTooLarge
117		}
118	
119		payload := make([]byte, payloadLen)
120		copy(payload, data[HeaderSize:HeaderSize+int(payloadLen)])
121	
122		f.Version = version
123		f.Flags = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[5:7])
124		f.Kind = data[7]
125		f.Payload = payload
126		return f, nil
127	}

1	package codec
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/binary"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"hash/crc32"
8		"os"
9		"path/filepath"
10		"sync"
11		"sync/atomic"
12	)
13	
14	// Reliable transport on top of the multi-frame Session.
15	//
16	// This layer adds sequence numbers, cumulative acknowledgements and a
17	// sliding-window pipeline. It does not touch the wire encoding of the
18	// layer below: every reliable message is carried inside the Payload of
19	// one ordinary codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope. The
20	// Encode/Decode entries, the header constants and the four existing
21	// error values keep their exact byte-level semantics.
22	//
23	// Envelope layout inside a codec frame payload (all multi-byte fields
24	// big-endian):
25	//
26	//		+---------+---------+--------+----------+---------+----------+=========+
27	//		| seq (4) | ack (4) | type(1)| flags(2) | kind(1) | crc32(4) | payload |
28	//		+---------+---------+--------+----------+---------+----------+=========+
29	//
30	//	  - seq: sender-assigned data sequence; ACK frames carry no data seq.
31	//	  - ack: cumulative acknowledgement as a "next expected" count: every
32	//	    data frame with seq < ack has been delivered to the reader.
33	//	  - type: 1 = data, 2 = pure acknowledgement.
34	//	  - flags/kind: the caller frame's Flags and Kind, carried inside the
35	//	    envelope; the outer codec Kind is a fixed marker of this layer.
36	//	  - crc32: IEEE CRC of the other 12 envelope bytes plus the payload.
37	//
38	// The underlying frame's payload limit stays MaxPayload; EnvelopeSize
39	// bytes are reserved, so the inner payload limit is ReliableMaxPayload.
40	//
41	// Delivery guarantees, across disconnects and sender-side restarts:
42	//   - Write side: frames are numbered in write order and streamed
43	//     through a fixed send window. Written frames are journaled in a
44	//     CRC'd replay log; the acknowledged position is recorded in a
45	//     dual-slot checkpoint. After a restart, sending resumes after the
46	//     earliest confirmed position recorded by either file, so an
47	//     acknowledged frame is never counted twice and no frame past it is
48	//     skipped (a resupplied frame is deduped on arrival).
49	//   - Read side: frames are delivered in sequence order exactly once.
50	//     A duplicate of an already delivered or already held frame is
51	//     acknowledged again but delivered once; an in-order gap closed by
52	//     an out-of-order arrival flushes the held run in order; a sequence
53	//     older than the window's duplicate span or more than one window
54	//     width ahead is refused and delivery stops at the current
55	//     position.
56	const (
57		// EnvelopeSize is this layer's per-frame overhead:
58		// 4 (seq) + 4 (ack) + 1 (type) + 2 (flags) + 1 (kind) + 4 (crc32).
59		EnvelopeSize = 16
60	
61		// ReliableMaxPayload is the largest inner payload a reliable data
62		// frame may carry; EnvelopeSize bytes are reserved inside the
63		// underlying frame, whose own limit stays MaxPayload.
64		ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize
65	
66		// envelope field offsets.
67		envSeqOff   = 0
68		envAckOff   = 4
69		envTypeOff  = 8
70		envFlagsOff = 9
71		envKindOff  = 11
72		envCRCOff   = 12
73		envBodyOff  = 16
74	)
75	
76	const (
77		envTypeData = 1
78		envTypeAck  = 2
79	
80		// outerKind is the codec-frame Kind of every reliable message; the
81		// caller's Kind travels inside the envelope and is never confused
82		// with this marker.
83		outerKind uint8 = 0xA5
84	)
85	
86	// ErrWindowFull is the established over-limit value a write returns when
87	// the send window already holds the maximum number of unacknowledged
88	// frames. It is the same sentinel the single-frame encoder uses for an
89	// over-limit payload: an over-window write is an over-limit write, and
90	// the offered frame is dropped without entering the window or the log
91	// and without consuming a sequence number.
92	var ErrWindowFull = ErrTooLarge
93	
94	// ReliableFrame is one caller-visible frame on the reliable layer.
95	type ReliableFrame struct {
96		Flags   uint16
97		Kind    uint8
98		Payload []byte
99	}
100	
101	// envelope is one parsed reliable message.
102	type envelope struct {
103		seq     uint32
104		ack     uint32
105		typ     uint8
106		flags   uint16
107		kind    uint8
108		payload []byte
109	}
110	
111	// encodeEnvelope serializes one message into the payload bytes of an
112	// ordinary codec frame.
113	func encodeEnvelope(e envelope) ([]byte, error) {
114		if e.typ == envTypeData && len(e.payload) > ReliableMaxPayload {
115			return nil, ErrTooLarge
116		}
117		out := make([]byte, EnvelopeSize+len(e.payload))
118		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envSeqOff:envSeqOff+4], e.seq)
119		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envAckOff:envAckOff+4], e.ack)
120		out[envTypeOff] = e.typ
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[envFlagsOff:envFlagsOff+2], e.flags)
122		out[envKindOff] = e.kind
123		copy(out[envBodyOff:], e.payload)
124		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
125		h.Write(out[:envCRCOff])
126		h.Write(out[envBodyOff:])
127		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envCRCOff:envCRCOff+4], h.Sum32())
128		return out, nil
129	}
130	
131	// decodeEnvelope parses one message from a codec frame payload. A
132	// damaged envelope is reported with the established checksum value;
133	// nothing is delivered from it.
134	func decodeEnvelope(p []byte) (envelope, error) {
135		var e envelope
136		if len(p) < EnvelopeSize {
137			return e, ErrShortFrame
138		}
139		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
140		h.Write(p[:envCRCOff])
141		h.Write(p[envBodyOff:])
142		if h.Sum32() != binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envCRCOff:envCRCOff+4]) {
143			return e, ErrChecksum
144		}
145		e.seq = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envSeqOff : envSeqOff+4])
146		e.ack = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envAckOff : envAckOff+4])
147		e.typ = p[envTypeOff]
148		e.flags = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(p[envFlagsOff : envFlagsOff+2])
149		e.kind = p[envKindOff]
150		body := make([]byte, len(p)-EnvelopeSize)
151		copy(body, p[EnvelopeSize:])
152		e.payload = body
153		return e, nil
154	}

156	// ReliableConfig configures a ReliableSession.
157	type ReliableConfig struct {
158		// Window is the send and receive window width in frames. It must be
159		// positive. Both peers of one connection should use the same width.
160		Window int
161	
162		// StateDir holds the checkpoint file and replay log used to resume
163		// the write side after a restart. It is created if missing.
164		StateDir string
165	}
166	
167	// ReliableSession is a reliability layer wrapping one Session. Create it
168	// with NewReliable; the wrapped session must not be used directly while
169	// the ReliableSession owns it.
170	//
171	// The two directions are independent and may be used concurrently, like
172	// the underlying session. A writer that wants the peer's
173	// acknowledgements to advance its window must let ReadFrame run
174	// (acknowledgements are consumed there, in a dedicated goroutine when
175	// traffic is one-directional).
176	type ReliableSession struct {
177		sess *Session
178		cfg  ReliableConfig
179	
180		wmu sync.Mutex
181		// sendBase is the oldest sequence not yet acknowledged (as a
182		// next-expected ack value); sendNext is the next sequence a newly
183		// written frame gets. Slot i holds sequence sendBase+i while it is
184		// unacknowledged.
185		sendBase uint32
186		sendNext uint32
187		window   []windowSlot
188		log      *replayLog
189		closed   bool
190	
191		rmu sync.Mutex
192		// recvBase is the next sequence due for delivery. It is atomic so the
193		// send paths (Flush, the ack pump) can read the position without
194		// taking rmu: ReadFrame must keep rmu free while blocked in the
195		// underlying reader, otherwise two peers reading at once deadlock.
196		recvBase atomic.Uint32
197		// held parks frames that arrived in-window but ahead of order; it is
198		// guarded by rmu.
199		held map[uint32]ReliableFrame
200		rerr error
201	
202		// ackCh is a coalescing signal: every delivery that moves recvBase
203		// (or repeats a duplicate the sender is still resending) pokes it
204		// non-blockingly, and pumpAck flushes one cumulative acknowledgement
205		// for the latest position. A capacity of 1 is enough because acks
206		// are cumulative. Keeping the write off the read path means two
207		// peers reading at the same time cannot block each other.
208		ackCh  chan struct{}
209		stopCh chan struct{}
210		doneCh chan struct{}
211	}
212	
213	type windowSlot struct {
214		used bool
215		seq  uint32
216		f    ReliableFrame
217	}
218	
219	// NewReliable wraps sess in a reliable session. Write state in
220	// cfg.StateDir is consulted when present: a fresh directory starts at
221	// sequence 0, while a directory left by a crashed or restarted process
222	// resumes from the earliest confirmed position held by its checkpoint
223	// and replay log.
224	//
225	// A checkpoint record torn by a crash mid-write fails its own checksum
226	// and is ignored in favor of the previous complete record. A replayed
227	// log that is truncated or contains a flipped bit fails with
228	// ErrChecksum.
229	func NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error) {
230		if cfg.Window <= 0 {
231			return nil, errors.New("codec: reliable window must be positive")
232		}
233		if cfg.StateDir == "" {
234			return nil, errors.New("codec: reliable session requires a state directory")
235		}
236		if err := os.MkdirAll(cfg.StateDir, 0o755); err != nil {
237			return nil, err
238		}
239	
240		rs := &ReliableSession{
241			sess:   sess,
242			cfg:    cfg,
243			window: make([]windowSlot, cfg.Window),
244			held:   make(map[uint32]ReliableFrame),
245			ackCh:  make(chan struct{}, 1),
246			stopCh: make(chan struct{}),
247			doneCh: make(chan struct{}),
248		}
249	
250		// Newest valid checkpoint record; a torn record is invisible here.
251		cpAck, _, err := loadCheckpoint(cfg.StateDir)
252		if err != nil {
253			return nil, err
254		}
255	
256		rs.log, err = openReplayLog(cfg.StateDir)
257		if err != nil {
258			return nil, err
259		}
260	
261		logBase, logNext, logEmpty := rs.log.bounds()
262		switch {
263		case logEmpty || cpAck >= logNext:
264			// Either there is nothing left to replay, or the checkpoint
265			// confirms a position at/beyond the log's tail (the journaled
266			// records are all older, already-delivered frames). Resume at the
267			// checkpoint: numbering new frames any earlier would collide with
268			// sequences the peer already received.
269			rs.sendBase = cpAck
270			rs.sendNext = cpAck
271		default:
272			// Log tail extends past the checkpoint. Resume at the log's
273			// first replayable frame. A checkpoint is durably written BEFORE
274			// its log prefix is discarded, so a crash can leave a log that
275			// still reaches further back than the checkpoint; resending that
276			// overlap is safe because the receiver deduplicates it. Starting
277			// any later would skip a frame that was never confirmed; starting
278			// earlier than logBase is impossible because those frames were
279			// already discarded by a confirmed checkpoint.
280			rs.sendBase = logBase
281			// sendNext stays one past the last journaled frame. A replay
282			// backlog wider than the window drains as acks advance and the
283			// freed tail slots are refilled from the log.
284			rs.sendNext = logNext
285		}
286	
287		rs.reloadWindow()
288		// Start the ack pump only after every error-return path is past: on
289		// a failed NewReliable no session (and no pump goroutine) exists.
290		go rs.pumpAck()
291		return rs, nil
292	}
293	
294	// reloadWindow refills the in-memory window slots from the replay log
295	// after a restart, so the first Flush resends every frame past the
296	// resume point.
297	func (rs *ReliableSession) reloadWindow() {
298		for i := range rs.window {
299			rs.window[i] = windowSlot{}
300		}
301		for _, rec := range rs.log.framesFrom(rs.sendBase) {
302			idx := int(rec.seq - rs.sendBase)
303			if idx >= len(rs.window) {
304				break
305			}
306			rs.window[idx] = windowSlot{used: true, seq: rec.seq, f: rec.f}
307		}
308	}
309	
310	// WriteFrame numbers f with the next send sequence, journals it and
311	// parks it in the send window. Nothing is transmitted before Flush.
312	// When the window already holds Window unacknowledged frames, WriteFrame
313	// returns ErrWindowFull (the established over-limit value) and drops the
314	// frame: it is neither windowed nor journaled and consumes no sequence.
315	// An oversized inner payload returns ErrTooLarge before anything else.
316	func (rs *ReliableSession) WriteFrame(f ReliableFrame) error {
317		if len(f.Payload) > ReliableMaxPayload {
318			return ErrTooLarge
319		}
320		rs.wmu.Lock()
321		defer rs.wmu.Unlock()
322	
323		if rs.closed {
324			return errors.New("codec: write on closed reliable session")
325		}
326		if rs.sendNext-rs.sendBase >= uint32(rs.cfg.Window) {
327			return ErrWindowFull
328		}
329	
330		seq := rs.sendNext
331		if err := rs.log.append(seq, f); err != nil {
332			return err
333		}
334		rs.window[int(seq-rs.sendBase)] = windowSlot{used: true, seq: seq, f: f}
335		rs.sendNext++
336		return nil
337	}
338	
339	// Flush sends every windowed frame in sequence order, each carrying the
340	// read side's current delivered position as a cumulative ack, followed
341	// by one pure acknowledgement, and flushes the wrapped session.
342	//
343	// Retransmission is a plain Flush on a restarted writer: the window was
344	// reloaded from the replay log, so Flush resends every frame past the
345	// resume point; the reader delivers each at most once.
346	func (rs *ReliableSession) Flush() error {
347		// recvBase is atomic, so no read lock is taken here: Flush never
348		// blocks a concurrent ReadFrame and vice versa.
349		ack := rs.recvBase.Load()
350	
351		rs.wmu.Lock()
352		out := make([]Frame, 0, len(rs.window)+1)
353		for i := range rs.window {
354			sl := &rs.window[i]
355			if !sl.used {
356				continue
357			}
358			b, err := encodeEnvelope(envelope{
359				seq:     sl.seq,
360				ack:     ack,
361				typ:     envTypeData,
362				flags:   sl.f.Flags,
363				kind:    sl.f.Kind,
364				payload: sl.f.Payload,
365			})
366			if err != nil {
367				rs.wmu.Unlock()
368				return err
369			}
370			out = append(out, Frame{Kind: outerKind, Payload: b})
371		}
372		out = append(out, rs.ackFrameLocked(ack))
373		rs.wmu.Unlock()
374	
375		for i := range out {
376			if err := rs.sess.WriteFrame(out[i]); err != nil {
377				return err
378			}
379		}
380		return rs.sess.Flush()
381	}
382	
383	// ackFrameLocked builds a pure acknowledgement. Caller holds wmu; the
384	// envelope's own seq is zero because ACK frames carry no data sequence.
385	func (rs *ReliableSession) ackFrameLocked(ack uint32) Frame {
386		b, _ := encodeEnvelope(envelope{ack: ack, typ: envTypeAck})
387		return Frame{Kind: outerKind, Payload: b}
388	}
389	
390	// ReadFrame returns the next in-order caller frame, exactly once. It
391	// internally processes reliable messages: acknowledgements (pure ones
392	// and piggybacked ones) advance the send window, duplicates are
393	// re-acknowledged but not redelivered, and in-window out-of-order frames
394	// are held until the gap closes and then delivered as a contiguous run.
395	// A sequence outside the window's reach - a residual older than the
396	// duplicate span or a declared sequence more than one window width
397	// ahead - is refused with ErrChecksum and delivery stops at the last
398	// in-order frame; the refusal is sticky.
399	func (rs *ReliableSession) ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error) {
400		for {
401			rs.rmu.Lock()
402			if rs.rerr != nil {
403				err := rs.rerr
404				rs.rmu.Unlock()
405				return ReliableFrame{}, err
406			}
407			// A contiguous held frame can be delivered without another read.
408			if f, ok := rs.held[rs.recvBase.Load()]; ok {
409				base := rs.recvBase.Load()
410				delete(rs.held, base)
411				rs.recvBase.Store(base + 1)
412				rs.signalAck()
413				rs.rmu.Unlock()
414				return f, nil
415			}
416			rs.rmu.Unlock()
417	
418			// Block in the underlying reader WITHOUT holding rmu: the read
419			// may wait indefinitely for bytes, and the send paths must stay
420			// able to observe recvBase meanwhile. The wrapped session
421			// serializes concurrent readers, so each wakeup owns one frame.
422			outer, rerr := rs.sess.ReadFrame()
423	
424			rs.rmu.Lock()
425			// Another reader may have recorded a terminal result while this
426			// one was blocked in the underlying read.
427			if rs.rerr != nil {
428				err := rs.rerr
429				rs.rmu.Unlock()
430				return ReliableFrame{}, err
431			}
432			if rerr != nil {
433				// Outer-layer results (io.EOF, a corrupt outer frame, a
434				// truncated trailing frame, an underlying reader error) pass
435				// through with their established values.
436				return rs.failReadLocked(rerr)
437			}
438	
439			env, err := decodeEnvelope(outer.Payload)
440			if err != nil {
441				return rs.failReadLocked(err)
442			}
443	
444			// Every inbound message may carry a cumulative acknowledgement
445			// for data we sent.
446			rs.applyAck(env.ack)
447	
448			if env.typ == envTypeAck {
449				rs.rmu.Unlock()
450				continue
451			}
452			if env.typ != envTypeData {
453				// An unknown message type cannot be placed in the ordered
454				// stream; refuse it like a damaged envelope.
455				return rs.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf("codec: unknown reliable message type %d: %w", env.typ, ErrChecksum))
456			}
457	
458			rf := ReliableFrame{Flags: env.flags, Kind: env.kind, Payload: env.payload}
459			base := rs.recvBase.Load()
460	
461			switch classify(env.seq, base, rs.cfg.Window) {
462			case seqInWindow:
463				if _, dup := rs.held[env.seq]; !dup {
464					// First arrival: park it. A retransmission of the same
465					// parked frame keeps the first copy.
466					rs.held[env.seq] = rf
467				}
468				// Restate the cumulative position either way (a fresh frame
469				// extends it only after in-order delivery; the duplicate case
470				// needs it so the peer stops resending).
471				rs.signalAck()
472				rs.rmu.Unlock()
473				continue // deliver held[recvBase] from the top of the loop
474			case seqDuplicate:
475				// Already delivered in an earlier call - a resend after its
476				// acknowledgement was lost. Do not deliver again; restate the
477				// cumulative position.
478				rs.signalAck()
479				rs.rmu.Unlock()
480				continue
481			case seqStale:
482				// Older than the duplicate span, or more than a window width
483				// ahead: refuse and stop where delivery currently is.
484				return rs.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf("codec: sequence %d outside window at %d (width %d): %w",
485					env.seq, base, rs.cfg.Window, ErrChecksum))
486			}
487		}
488	}
489	
490	type seqClass int
491	
492	const (
493		seqDuplicate seqClass = iota // behind base, within one window width
494		seqInWindow                  // [base, base+Window)
495		seqStale                     // anywhere else: ancient residual or too far ahead
496	)
497	
498	// classify positions an inbound sequence relative to a receive window
499	// starting at base. uint32 modular subtraction keeps the check correct
500	// across sequence wraparound.
501	func classify(seq, base uint32, window int) seqClass {
502		if fwd := seq - base; fwd < uint32(window) {
503			return seqInWindow
504		}
505		if back := base - seq; back >= 1 && back <= uint32(window) {
506			return seqDuplicate
507		}
508		return seqStale
509	}
510	
511	// signalAck coalescingly asks the ack pump to restate recvBase. It never
512	// blocks and never writes from under the read lock.
513	func (rs *ReliableSession) signalAck() {
514		select {
515		case rs.ackCh <- struct{}{}:
516		default:
517		}
518	}
519	
520	// pumpAck serializes all standalone acknowledgement writes. One poke
521	// yields at most one ack stating the latest delivered position, so a
522	// burst of deliveries sends a few cumulative acks rather than one per
523	// frame. Writes happen on this goroutine, not on the caller's read
524	// goroutine, which is what lets two peers read simultaneously without
525	// deadlocking.
526	func (rs *ReliableSession) pumpAck() {
527		defer close(rs.doneCh)
528		for {
529			select {
530			case <-rs.stopCh:
531				return
532			case <-rs.ackCh:
533			}
534	
535			// Coalesce pokes that accumulated while the previous ack was
536			// being written.
537			select {
538			case <-rs.ackCh:
539			default:
540			}
541	
542			ack := rs.recvBase.Load()
543			rs.wmu.Lock()
544			frame := rs.ackFrameLocked(ack)
545			rs.wmu.Unlock()
546			// Best effort: a failed or blocked ack is harmless because every
547			// later Flush piggybacks the same cumulative position.
548			if err := rs.sess.WriteFrame(frame); err == nil {
549				_ = rs.sess.Flush()
550			}
551		}
552	}
553	
554	// applyAck advances the send window past a cumulative "next expected"
555	// acknowledgement and makes the new position durable. Called with rmu
556	// held; takes wmu (rmu-then-wmu order).
557	func (rs *ReliableSession) applyAck(ack uint32) {
558		rs.wmu.Lock()
559		defer rs.wmu.Unlock()
560	
561		// ack states that every seq < ack is delivered. Ignore values that
562		// do not move the window forward or pass the highest numbered seq.
563		if ack <= rs.sendBase || ack > rs.sendNext {
564			return
565		}
566		shift := ack - rs.sendBase
567		if shift > uint32(len(rs.window)) {
568			shift = uint32(len(rs.window))
569		}
570	
571		// Slide occupied slots down; sources are always read at higher
572		// indices than the destination, so overlap cannot erase an unread
573		// slot.
574		for i := 0; i+int(shift) < len(rs.window); i++ {
575			rs.window[i] = rs.window[i+int(shift)]
576		}
577		for i := len(rs.window) - int(shift); i < len(rs.window); i++ {
578			rs.window[i] = windowSlot{}
579		}
580		rs.sendBase += shift
581	
582		// After a restart the replay backlog may be wider than the window:
583		// the freed tail slots are refilled from the log as the window
584		// advances, so every journaled frame eventually goes out.
585		rs.reloadWindow()
586	
587		// Make the new position durable BEFORE discarding the journaled
588		// prefix: a crash between the two leaves extra replayable frames
589		// (deduped on resend), never a gap. Prefix only after the checkpoint
590		// actually landed: a failed checkpoint plus a successful prefix would
591		// otherwise be the one ordering that can lose frames.
592		if err := saveCheckpoint(rs.cfg.StateDir, rs.sendBase); err == nil && rs.log != nil {
593			_ = rs.log.prefix(rs.sendBase)
594		}
595	}
596	
597	// failReadLocked records the terminal read-side result, releases rmu and
598	// returns it. Every caller returns immediately after calling it.
599	func (rs *ReliableSession) failReadLocked(err error) (ReliableFrame, error) {
600		rs.rerr = err
601		rs.rmu.Unlock()
602		return ReliableFrame{}, err
603	}
604	
605	// Close marks the session closed and asks the acknowledgement pump to
606	// stop; a pump blocked on an unread transport unwinds once that
607	// transport is closed. Fully journaled but unacknowledged frames remain
608	// in the replay log for a later restart to resend.
609	func (rs *ReliableSession) Close() error {
610		rs.wmu.Lock()
611		if rs.closed {
612			rs.wmu.Unlock()
613			return nil
614		}
615		rs.closed = true
616		rs.wmu.Unlock()
617		close(rs.stopCh)
618		return nil
619	}
620	
621	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
622	// Durable state: a dual-slot, checksummed checkpoint and a strict,
623	// CRC'd replay log.
624	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
625	
626	// Checkpoint: two fixed, independently checksummed records in one file.
627	// Every save writes the ALTERNATE slot with a strictly higher
628	// generation, so a crash mid-write leaves the previous complete record
629	// intact in the other slot; on load the highest-generation record that
630	// validates wins.
631	const (
632		checkpointName = "reliable.ckp"
633		cpRecordSize   = 4 + 4 + 4 // generation + ack + crc32
634		cpSlotCount    = 2
635		checkpointSize = cpRecordSize * cpSlotCount
636	)
637	
638	type cpRecord struct {
639		generation uint32
640		ack        uint32
641	}
642	
643	func checkpointPath(dir string) string {
644		return filepath.Join(dir, checkpointName)
645	}
646	
647	func marshalCPRecord(r cpRecord) []byte {
648		b := make([]byte, cpRecordSize)
649		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[0:4], r.generation)
650		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[4:8], r.ack)
651		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[8:12], crc32.ChecksumIEEE(b[0:8]))
652		return b
653	}
654	
655	func unmarshalCPRecord(b []byte) (cpRecord, bool) {
656		var r cpRecord
657		if len(b) < cpRecordSize {
658			return r, false
659		}
660		if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[8:12]) != crc32.ChecksumIEEE(b[0:8]) {
661			return r, false
662		}
663		r.generation = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[0:4])
664		r.ack = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[4:8])
665		return r, true
666	}
667	
668	// loadCheckpoint returns the acknowledged "next expected" position of
669	// the newest valid record. A missing/empty file, or one whose records
670	// all fail validation, means "no checkpoint yet" (position 0): with no
671	// confirmed position the safe action is to replay everything the log
672	// holds, and the reader deduplicates the overlap.
673	func loadCheckpoint(dir string) (uint32, bool, error) {
674		data, err := os.ReadFile(checkpointPath(dir))
675		if err != nil {
676			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
677				return 0, false, nil
678			}
679			return 0, false, err
680		}
681		if len(data) == 0 {
682			return 0, false, nil
683		}
684	
685		var best cpRecord
686		found := false
687		for off := 0; off+cpRecordSize <= len(data); off += cpRecordSize {
688			if r, ok := unmarshalCPRecord(data[off : off+cpRecordSize]); ok {
689				if !found || r.generation > best.generation ||
690					(r.generation == best.generation && r.ack > best.ack) {
691					best = r
692					found = true
693				}
694			}
695		}
696		if !found {
697			return 0, false, nil
698		}
699		return best.ack, true, nil
700	}
701	
702	// nextCPSlot chooses the slot to overwrite and the next generation:
703	// alternate slots, strictly increasing generations.
704	func nextCPSlot(dir string) (slot int, generation uint32, err error) {
705		data, rerr := os.ReadFile(checkpointPath(dir))
706		if rerr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rerr) {
707			return 0, 0, rerr
708		}
709		var gens [cpSlotCount]uint32
710		var ok [cpSlotCount]bool
711		for i := 0; i < cpSlotCount; i++ {
712			lo, hi := i*cpRecordSize, (i+1)*cpRecordSize
713			if len(data) >= hi {
714				if r, valid := unmarshalCPRecord(data[lo:hi]); valid {
715					gens[i], ok[i] = r.generation, true
716				}
717			}
718		}
719		switch {
720		case !ok[0] && !ok[1]:
721			return 0, 1, nil
722		case ok[0] && (!ok[1] || gens[0] >= gens[1]):
723			return 1, gens[0] + 1, nil
724		default:
725			return 0, gens[1] + 1, nil
726		}
727	}
728	
729	// saveCheckpoint writes one new record into the alternate slot. The
730	// other slot is untouched, so at every durable instant at least the
731	// previous complete record survives. The very first write sizes the
732	// file to both slots; later writes never touch the slot they are not
733	// rewriting.
734	func saveCheckpoint(dir string, ack uint32) error {
735		slot, generation, err := nextCPSlot(dir)
736		if err != nil {
737			return err
738		}
739		path := checkpointPath(dir)
740	
741		// Size the file before the record write so the padding never lands
742		// on a slot an earlier checkpoint already filled.
743		needPad := true
744		if info, statErr := os.Stat(path); statErr == nil && info.Size() >= checkpointSize {
745			needPad = false
746		}
747	
748		f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o644)
749		if err != nil {
750			return err
751		}
752		defer f.Close()
753	
754		if needPad {
755			if _, err := f.WriteAt(make([]byte, checkpointSize), 0); err != nil {
756				return err
757			}
758		}
759		if _, err := f.WriteAt(marshalCPRecord(cpRecord{generation: generation, ack: ack}),
760			int64(slot*cpRecordSize)); err != nil {
761			return err
762		}
763		return f.Sync()
764	}
765	
766	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
767	// Replay log: appended, length-prefixed, CRC'd records in sequence
768	// order. Scanning is strict: every byte must belong to one complete,
769	// valid record. A truncated file or a flipped bit therefore fails with
770	// ErrChecksum instead of silently delivering or skipping frames.
771	//
772	// Record layout:
773	//
774	//	+---------+---------+----------+--------+----------+=========+
775	//	| seq (4) | kind(1) | flags(2) | len(4) | crc32(4) | payload |
776	//	+---------+---------+----------+--------+----------+=========+
777	//
778	// The CRC covers the 11 header bytes and the payload.
779	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
780	
781	const (
782		logName    = "reliable.log"
783		logHdrSize = 4 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 4
784	)
785	
786	type logRecord struct {
787		seq uint32
788		f   ReliableFrame
789	}
790	
791	type replayLog struct {
792		path string
793		mu   sync.Mutex
794		recs []logRecord
795	}
796	
797	func openReplayLog(dir string) (*replayLog, error) {
798		l := &replayLog{path: filepath.Join(dir, logName)}
799		if err := l.load(); err != nil {
800			return nil, err
801		}
802		return l, nil
803	}
804	
805	func (l *replayLog) load() error {
806		data, err := os.ReadFile(l.path)
807		if err != nil {
808			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
809				return nil
810			}
811			return err
812		}
813	
814		for off := 0; off < len(data); {
815			// Any bytes that do not form a complete, valid record are a
816			// truncated tail: strict failure, no further delivery.
817			if len(data)-off < logHdrSize {
818				return fmt.Errorf("codec: replay log %s truncated: %w", logName, ErrChecksum)
819			}
820			hdr := data[off : off+logHdrSize]
821			seq := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[0:4])
822			kind := hdr[4]
823			flags := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(hdr[5:7])
824			plen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[7:11]))
825			wantCRC := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[11:15])
826	
827			end := off + logHdrSize + plen
828			if plen < 0 || end > len(data) {
829				return fmt.Errorf("codec: replay log %s truncated: %w", logName, ErrChecksum)
830			}
831			h := crc32.NewIEEE()
832			h.Write(hdr[:11])
833			h.Write(data[off+logHdrSize : end])
834			if h.Sum32() != wantCRC {
835				return fmt.Errorf("codec: replay log %s corrupted: %w", logName, ErrChecksum)
836			}
837	
838			payload := make([]byte, plen)
839			copy(payload, data[off+logHdrSize:end])
840			l.recs = append(l.recs, logRecord{
841				seq: seq,
842				f:   ReliableFrame{Flags: flags, Kind: kind, Payload: payload},
843			})
844			off = end
845		}
846		return nil
847	}
848	
849	// append journals one frame as a single fully checksummed record.
850	func (l *replayLog) append(seq uint32, f ReliableFrame) error {
851		l.mu.Lock()
852		defer l.mu.Unlock()
853	
854		hdr := make([]byte, logHdrSize)
855		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[0:4], seq)
856		hdr[4] = f.Kind
857		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(hdr[5:7], f.Flags)
858		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[7:11], uint32(len(f.Payload)))
859		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
860		h.Write(hdr[:11])
861		h.Write(f.Payload)
862		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[11:15], h.Sum32())
863	
864		file, err := os.OpenFile(l.path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
865		if err != nil {
866			return err
867		}
868		// One write of the whole record keeps the on-disk tail either absent
869		// or complete from the point of view of a killing crash.
870		if _, err := file.Write(append(hdr, f.Payload...)); err != nil {
871			file.Close()
872			return err
873		}
874		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
875			file.Close()
876			return err
877		}
878		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {
879			return err
880		}
881	
882		l.recs = append(l.recs, logRecord{seq: seq, f: f})
883		return nil
884	}
885	
886	// bounds reports the lowest and one-past-the-highest held sequence and
887	// whether the log is empty.
888	func (l *replayLog) bounds() (base, next uint32, empty bool) {
889		l.mu.Lock()
890		defer l.mu.Unlock()
891		if len(l.recs) == 0 {
892			return 0, 0, true
893		}
894		return l.recs[0].seq, l.recs[len(l.recs)-1].seq + 1, false
895	}
896	
897	// framesFrom returns the logged frames with sequence >= from, in order.
898	func (l *replayLog) framesFrom(from uint32) []logRecord {
899		l.mu.Lock()
900		defer l.mu.Unlock()
901		var out []logRecord
902		for _, r := range l.recs {
903			if r.seq >= from {
904				out = append(out, r)
905			}
906		}
907		return out
908	}

910	// prefix discards logged frames with sequence < base (already
911	// acknowledged), rewriting the log atomically via temp file + rename.
912	func (l *replayLog) prefix(base uint32) error {
913		l.mu.Lock()
914		defer l.mu.Unlock()
915	
916		keep := l.recs[:0]
917		for _, r := range l.recs {
918			if r.seq >= base {
919				keep = append(keep, r)
920			}
921		}
922		if len(keep) == len(l.recs) {
923			return nil
924		}
925		l.recs = keep
926	
927		tmp := l.path + ".tmp"
928		f, err := os.OpenFile(tmp, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
929		if err != nil {
930			return err
931		}
932		for _, r := range keep {
933			hdr := make([]byte, logHdrSize)
934			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[0:4], r.seq)
935			hdr[4] = r.f.Kind
936			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(hdr[5:7], r.f.Flags)
937			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[7:11], uint32(len(r.f.Payload)))
938			h := crc32.NewIEEE()
939			h.Write(hdr[:11])
940			h.Write(r.f.Payload)
941			binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(hdr[11:15], h.Sum32())
942			if _, err := f.Write(hdr); err != nil {
943				f.Close()
944				return err
945			}
946			if _, err := f.Write(r.f.Payload); err != nil {
947				f.Close()
948				return err
949			}
950		}
951		if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {
952			f.Close()
953			return err
954		}
955		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
956			return err
957		}
958		return os.Rename(tmp, l.path)
959	}

3	import (
4		"encoding/binary"
5		"io"
6		"sync"
7	)
8	
9	// flusher is implemented by buffered writers such as *bufio.Writer.
10	type flusher interface {
11		Flush() error
12	}
13	
14	// Session is a concurrency-safe multi-frame layer sitting on top of one
15	// byte writer and one byte reader. It does not change the wire format:
16	// every written frame is serialized with Encode and frames are simply
17	// concatenated, so the byte stream stays byte-for-byte compatible with
18	// the single-frame Encode/Decode entries.
19	//
20	// The two directions are independent and may be used concurrently:
21	//   - WriteFrame appends one whole encoded frame to an internal write
22	//     buffer; Flush writes everything buffered so far, in write order,
23	//     to the underlying writer.
24	//   - ReadFrame pulls bytes from the underlying reader in whatever
25	//     chunk sizes they arrive, keeps an incomplete trailing frame in an
26	//     internal buffer and returns one complete Frame per call.
27	//
28	// The total number of frames in a session is unbounded; the per-frame
29	// payload limit is MaxPayload, enforced at write time.
30	type Session struct {
31		w io.Writer
32		r io.Reader
33	
34		wmu  sync.Mutex
35		wbuf []byte
36	
37		rmu  sync.Mutex
38		rbuf []byte
39		// terminal error of the read side: a bad frame's error, io.EOF or
40		// an error reported by the underlying reader.
41		rerr error
42	}
43	
44	// NewSession returns a session writing to w and reading from r.
45	func NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session {
46		return &Session{w: w, r: r}
47	}
48	
49	// WriteFrame encodes f with the single-frame encoder and appends the
50	// whole frame to the session's write buffer. Because Encode rejects an
51	// oversized payload before any byte is buffered, an ErrTooLarge result
52	// never leaves a partial frame behind, and concurrent writes never
53	// interleave the bytes of one frame with another. Writes become visible
54	// to the reader in call-arrival order once Flush runs.
55	func (s *Session) WriteFrame(f Frame) error {
56		b, err := Encode(f)
57		if err != nil {
58			return err
59		}
60		s.wmu.Lock()
61		s.wbuf = append(s.wbuf, b...)
62		s.wmu.Unlock()
63		return nil
64	}
65	
66	// Flush writes every buffered frame to the underlying writer as one
67	// ordered run and then, if the writer implements Flush itself (for
68	// example *bufio.Writer), flushes it. Bytes already appended by
69	// WriteFrame are never reordered or split across frames. If the
70	// underlying writer errors after a short write, the unsent tail is
71	// retained and a later Flush retries it.
72	func (s *Session) Flush() error {
73		s.wmu.Lock()
74		defer s.wmu.Unlock()
75	
76		pending := s.wbuf
77		for len(pending) > 0 {
78			n, err := s.w.Write(pending)
79			pending = pending[n:]
80			if err != nil {
81				// Keep the unsent tail at the front of the buffer so a
82				// later WriteFrame/Flush continues from exactly this point.
83				copy(s.wbuf, pending)
84				s.wbuf = s.wbuf[:len(pending)]
85				return err
86			}
87		}
88		s.wbuf = s.wbuf[:0]
89	
90		if f, ok := s.w.(flusher); ok {
91			return f.Flush()
92		}
93		return nil
94	}
95	
96	// ReadFrame returns the next complete frame, reading more bytes from the
97	// underlying reader only when the buffer cannot yet supply one. A
98	// truncated frame at the end of the input is buffered without error
99	// until more bytes arrive; it is reported as ErrShortFrame only when the
100	// reader signals end of input with bytes still outstanding. A clean end
101	// of input with no residual bytes returns io.EOF, i.e. reading simply
102	// stops.
103	//
104	// When a complete frame is corrupt, the error is the same value Decode
105	// would return for that frame (ErrBadVersion, ErrChecksum or
106	// ErrTooLarge); frame delivery stops there and the error becomes
107	// sticky, while every frame returned earlier already belongs to the
108	// caller. Concurrent ReadFrame calls are serialized, so each frame is
109	// delivered exactly once.
110	func (s *Session) ReadFrame() (Frame, error) {
111		s.rmu.Lock()
112		defer s.rmu.Unlock()
113	
114		if s.rerr != nil {
115			return Frame{}, s.rerr
116		}
117	
118		var scratch [4096]byte
119	
120		for {
121			// A frame can be handed to Decode only once its declared length
122			// is fully buffered; Decode then decides every error with exactly
123			// the same precedence the single-frame entry uses.
124			if len(s.rbuf) >= HeaderSize {
125				frameLen := uint64(HeaderSize) + uint64(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(s.rbuf[0:4]))
126				if uint64(len(s.rbuf)) >= frameLen {
127					f, err := Decode(s.rbuf[:int(frameLen)])
128					if err != nil {
129						return s.failRead(err)
130					}
131					// Drop the consumed frame and compact the residual bytes
132					// of later frames to the front; Decode copied the payload
133					// out, so overlapping storage is safe.
134					rest := len(s.rbuf) - int(frameLen)
135					copy(s.rbuf, s.rbuf[int(frameLen):])
136					s.rbuf = s.rbuf[:rest]
137					return f, nil
138				}
139			}
140	
141			n, err := s.r.Read(scratch[:])
142			if n > 0 {
143				s.rbuf = append(s.rbuf, scratch[:n]...)
144			}
145			if err == nil {
146				// A (0, nil) read delivers no information; retry instead of
147				// mistaking it for end of input.
148				continue
149			}
150			if err == io.EOF {
151				if len(s.rbuf) > 0 {
152					return s.failRead(ErrShortFrame)
153				}
154				return s.failRead(io.EOF)
155			}
156			return s.failRead(err)
157		}
158	}
159	
160	// failRead records the terminal read-side error and returns it with the
161	// zero frame.
162	func (s *Session) failRead(err error) (Frame, error) {
163		s.rerr = err
164		return Frame{}, err
165	}

# frame-codec

Binary frame codec for a length-prefixed wire format, with a checksum, a version byte and precise errors for truncated or damaged input.

## Requirements

Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.

## Build

    go build ./...
    go run ./cmd/framedecode --file <path>

## Public interface

`codec.Encode(frame Frame) ([]byte, error)` returns the framed bytes.
- `codec.Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error)` returns the decoded frame.
- `type Frame struct { Version uint8; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte }`.
- `codec.HeaderSize`, `codec.MaxPayload` constants.
- `codec.ErrShortFrame`, `codec.ErrBadVersion`, `codec.ErrChecksum`, `codec.ErrTooLarge` error values.

## Multi-frame sessions

`codec.NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session` wraps one byte
writer and one byte reader in a concurrency-safe session. Frames are
just concatenated single-frame encodings, so the wire format and the
single-frame entries are unchanged.

- `(*Session).WriteFrame(Frame) error` appends one whole encoded frame
  in call-arrival order; an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`
  before any byte is buffered.
- `(*Session).Flush() error` writes everything buffered so far to the
  underlying writer (and flushes it when it implements `Flush` itself).
- `(*Session).ReadFrame() (Frame, error)` parses incrementally: complete
  frames are returned one per call while a trailing half frame stays
  buffered for later bytes. A clean end of input returns `io.EOF`; a
  truncated trailing frame returns `ErrShortFrame`; a corrupt frame
  returns the same value `Decode` would return for it and stops further
  delivery, with previously returned frames already in the caller's
  hands.

Reads and writes are independently serialized, so one session may be
shared by concurrent writers and readers; the bytes of a single frame
are never interleaved.

## Reliable sessions

`codec.NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error)`
wraps an existing session in a reliability layer. The lower wire format
is not changed: every reliable message is the payload of one ordinary
codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope, so `Encode`/`Decode`,
the header constants and the four established error values keep their
exact byte-level semantics.

- `ReliableConfig{Window int; StateDir string}`: send/receive window
  width in frames and a directory for write-side state (checkpoint and
  replay log); it is created if missing.
- `ReliableFrame{Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}` is the
  caller-visible frame. `EnvelopeSize` (16) bytes are reserved inside
  the underlying frame, so the inner payload limit is
  `ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize`.
- `(*ReliableSession).WriteFrame(ReliableFrame) error` numbers frames in
  write order, journals each one, and parks it in the send window;
  nothing goes out before `Flush`. When the window is full it returns
  the established over-limit value `ErrWindowFull` (the same sentinel as
  `ErrTooLarge`) and drops the frame without consuming a sequence. An
  oversized inner payload returns `ErrTooLarge`.
- `(*ReliableSession).Flush() error` sends all windowed frames in seq
  order, each piggybacking a cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement,
  plus one pure ack; on a restart the window is reloaded from the replay
  log, so `Flush` is also the retransmit operation.
- `(*ReliableSession).ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error)` delivers in seq
  order exactly once. Acks advance the send window; duplicates of
  delivered or parked frames are re-acknowledged but never redelivered;
  in-window out-of-order frames are parked and delivered as a contiguous
  run once the gap closes; a declared sequence outside the window's
  reach (an ancient residual older than one window width, or one width
  ahead of the current position) is refused with `ErrChecksum`, stopping
  delivery stickily at the current position. Outer-layer results
  (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size errors) pass
  through unchanged.

Standalone acks are written by a small background pump, so a writer
that needs the peer's acks to drain its window must let `ReadFrame` run
(or run it in a dedicated goroutine for one-directional traffic).

### Crash recovery

Written data frames are recorded in a CRC'd replay log (`reliable.log`);
the acknowledged position is recorded in a dual-slot checkpoint
(`reliable.ckp`), writing the alternate slot with a higher generation
each time:

- a checkpoint torn by a crash mid-write fails its own CRC and is
  ignored, falling back to the previous complete record;
- a truncated replay log, or a flipped bit in a complete record, fails
  recovery with `ErrChecksum` rather than delivering unverified frames;
- the checkpoint is made durable before the log prefix is discarded, so
  reconciliation always resumes from the earlier confirmed position: no
  acknowledged frame is resent past the peer's state, no unacknowledged
  frame is skipped, and the receiver deduplicates the overlap.

After recovery the first `Flush` re-sends every frame past the resume
point; backlogs wider than the window drain as acks refill the freed
tail slots from the log.

## Tests

    go test ./...

## Limits

Single frame in memory; no streaming reader in this scope.
No compression and no encryption.
Standard library only.

```go
func (m *Mux) Flush() error {
    m.wmu.Lock()
    for {
        ch := m.nextChannelLocked()
        if ch < 0 { break }
        c := &m.send[ch]
        q := c.queue[0]
        env := muxEnvelope{
            channel: uint16(ch),
            seq:     c.nextSeq,
            ack:     m.expect[ch].Load(),
            payload: q.payload,

        if q.fin { env.flags = muxFlagFIN }
        err := m.rs.WriteFrame(ReliableFrame{Flags: q.flags, Kind: q.kind, Payload: encodeMuxEnvelope(env)})
        if err == ErrWindowFull { break }
        if err != nil { m.wmu.Unlock(); return err }
        c.nextSeq++
        c.unacked = append(c.unacked, env.seq)
        c.queue = c.queue[1:]
        if len(c.queue) == 0 { c.queue = nil }
        m.rr = ch + 1
        m.ckpDirty = true
    }

    m.ckpDirty = false
    if dirty {
        if err := m.saveCheckpointLocked(); err != nil {
            m.wmu.Unlock()
            return err
        }
    }
    m.wmu.Unlock()
    return m.rs.Flush()
```

```go
        if m.rerr != nil {
            err := m.rerr
            m.rmu.Unlock()
            return MuxFrame{}, err
        }

            m.rmu.Unlock()
            if eof { return mf, io.EOF }
            return mf, nil

        if m.rerr != nil {
            err := m.rerr
            m.rmu.Unlock()
            return MuxFrame{}, err

        if rerr != nil {
            m.rmu.Unlock()
            return MuxFrame{}, rerr
        }
        env, err := decodeMuxEnvelope(rf.Payload)
        if err != nil {
            return m.failReadLocked(err)
        }
        if int(env.channel) >= m.cfg.Channels {
            return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d out of range [0,%d): %w", env.channel, m.cfg.Channels, ErrChecksum))
        }
        ch := env.channel

        if env.flags&muxFlagAck != 0 {

            continue

        p := muxParked{env: env, rfFlags: rf.Flags, rfKind: rf.Kind, hash: muxHash(rf.Flags, rf.Kind, env)}

                if err != nil {

                m.rmu.Unlock()
                if eof { return mf, io.EOF }
                return mf, nil
            }
            if old, dup := m.held[ch][env.seq]; dup {
                if old.hash != p.hash {
                    return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d seq %d conflicting retransmit: %w", ch, env.seq, ErrChecksum))

            return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d seq %d outside window at %d (quota %d): %w", ch, env.seq, expect, m.cfg.Quota, ErrChecksum))
        }
    }
```

```go
func (m *Mux) acceptLocked(ch uint16, p muxParked) (MuxFrame, bool, error) {
    if m.recvClosed[ch] {
        return MuxFrame{}, false, fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d seq %d arrives after channel close: %w", ch, p.env.seq, ErrChecksum)
    }
    seq := p.env.seq
    m.hist[ch][seq] = p.hash
    next := seq + 1
    m.expect[ch].Store(next)
    // trim history to the duplicate span
    for k := range m.hist[ch] {
        if d := next - k; d > uint32(m.cfg.Quota) && d < 1<<31 {
            delete(m.hist[ch], k)
        }
    }
    m.signalAckLocked(ch)
    if p.env.flags&muxFlagFIN != 0 {
        m.recvClosed[ch] = true
        return MuxFrame{Channel: ch}, true, nil
    }
    return MuxFrame{
        Channel: ch,
        Flags:   p.rfFlags,
        Kind:    p.rfKind,
        Payload: p.env.payload,
    }, false, nil
}
```

```go
func (m *Mux) saveCheckpointLocked() error {
    path := filepath.Join(m.dir, muxCheckpointName)
    recSize := muxCPRecordSize(m.cfg.Channels)
    // determine slot & generation from existing file
    var gens [2]uint32
    var ok [2]bool
    data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
    if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) { return err }
    for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
        lo, hi := i*recSize, (i+1)*recSize
        if len(data) >= hi {
            if g, _, valid := unmarshalMuxCP(data[lo:hi], m.cfg.Channels); valid {
                gens[i], ok[i] = g, true
            }
        }
    }
    var slot int
    var gen uint32
    switch {
    case !ok[0] && !ok[1]: slot, gen = 0, 1
    case ok[0] && (!ok[1] || gens[0] >= gens[1]): slot, gen = 1, gens[0]+1
    default: slot, gen = 0, gens[1]+1
    }
    d := muxCPData{next: make([]uint32, m.cfg.Channels), closed: make([]bool, m.cfg.Channels)}
    for i := range m.send {
        d.next[i] = m.send[i].nextSeq
        d.closed[i] = m.send[i].closed
    }
    f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o644)
    if err != nil { return err }
    defer f.Close()
    if info, statErr := f.Stat(); statErr == nil && info.Size() < int64(2*recSize) {
        if _, err := f.WriteAt(make([]byte, 2*recSize), 0); err != nil { return err }
    }
    if _, err := f.WriteAt(marshalMuxCP(gen, d), int64(slot*recSize)); err != nil { return err }
    return f.Sync()
}
```

marshal/unmarshal:

```go
func marshalMuxCP(gen uint32, d muxCPData) []byte {
    channels := len(d.next)
    b := make([]byte, muxCPRecordSize(channels))
    binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[0:4], gen)
    off := 4
    for _, n := range d.next {
        binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[off:off+4], n)
        off += 4
    }
    for i, c := range d.closed {
        if c { b[off+i/8] |= 1 << uint(i%8) }
    }
    off += (channels + 7) / 8
    binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[off:off+4], crc32.ChecksumIEEE(b[:off]))
    return b
}

func unmarshalMuxCP(b []byte, channels int) (uint32, muxCPData, bool) {
    var d muxCPData
    need := muxCPRecordSize(channels)
    if len(b) < need { return 0, d, false }
    off := 4 + 4*channels + (channels+7)/8
    if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[off:off+4]) != crc32.ChecksumIEEE(b[:off]) { return 0, d, false }
    d.next = make([]uint32, channels)
    d.closed = make([]bool, channels)
    p := 4
    for i := range d.next {
        d.next[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[p:p+4]); p += 4
    }
    for i := range d.closed {
        d.closed[i] = b[p+i/8]&(1<<uint(i%8)) != 0
    }
    return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[0:4]), d, true
}

func loadMuxCheckpoint(dir string, channels int) ([]uint32, []bool, error) {
    next := make([]uint32, channels)
    closed := make([]bool, channels)
    data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, muxCheckpointName))
    if err != nil {
        if os.IsNotExist(err) { return next, closed, nil }
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    recSize := muxCPRecordSize(channels)
    var bestGen uint32
    var best muxCPData
    found := false
    for off := 0; off+recSize <= len(data); off += recSize {
        if g, d, ok := unmarshalMuxCP(data[off:off+recSize], channels); ok {
            if !found || g > bestGen { bestGen, best, found = g, d, true }
        }
    }
    if found { return best.next, best.closed, nil }
    return next, closed, nil
}
```

29	//	+----------+---------+--------+---------+----------+=========+
30	//
31	//   - chan: the channel number the frame belongs to.
32	//   - seq: per-channel write sequence, numbered in write order; an ack
33	//     frame carries no data seq and sets it to zero.
34	//   - fl: 1 = FIN, the channel's closing frame (no payload, no caller
35	//     flags/kind); 2 = standalone cumulative acknowledgement. The two
36	//     are never combined.
37	//   - ack: cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement for chan,
38	//     piggybacked on every message: every data frame of chan with seq
39	//     < ack has been delivered to the reader.
40	//   - crc32: IEEE CRC of the other 11 header bytes plus the payload.
41	//
42	// The reliable frame's own payload limit stays ReliableMaxPayload;
43	// MuxHeaderSize bytes are reserved, so the inner payload limit is
44	// MuxMaxPayload.
45	//
46	// Delivery guarantees:
47	//   - Frames within one channel are delivered in write order exactly
48	//     once; channels are independent, so a gap on one channel never
49	//     blocks another channel's delivery.
50	//   - The send side hands transmission opportunities out round-robin
51	//     across channels, so one channel sending continuously can never
52	//     starve the others.
53	//   - Every channel has its own in-flight quota; a write that finds the
54	//     quota full returns the established over-limit value ErrWindowFull
55	//     and an oversized payload returns ErrTooLarge. A rejected frame is
56	//     neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it takes
57	//     no quota; the total buffer is bounded by Channels*Window frames.
58	//   - A channel opens on its first write and its write side can be
59	//     closed independently; its FIN rides the sequence stream like a
60	//     data frame. After the peer has received the channel's remaining
61	//     frames, the read that reaches the FIN returns io.EOF together with
62	//     a ChannelFrame naming the channel; other channels keep flowing.
63	//     Writing to, or closing, an already closed channel returns
64	//     ErrChannelClosed.
65	//
66	// As on the reliable layer, nothing is transmitted before Flush; after
67	// a restart the queue is reloaded from the journal, so Flush is also the
68	// retransmit operation.
69	const (
70		// MuxHeaderSize is this layer's per-frame overhead:
71		// 2 (chan) + 4 (seq) + 1 (flags) + 4 (ack) + 4 (crc32).
72		MuxHeaderSize = 2 + 4 + 1 + 4 + 4
73	
74		// MuxMaxPayload is the largest payload a multiplexed data frame may
75		// carry; MuxHeaderSize bytes are reserved inside the reliable
76		// payload, whose own limit stays ReliableMaxPayload.
77		MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize
78	
79		// mux header field offsets.
80		mhChanOff = 0
81		mhSeqOff  = 2
82		mhFlagOff = 6
83		mhAckOff  = 7
84		mhCRCOff  = 11
85		mhBodyOff = 15
86	
87		mhFlagFin = 1 << 0
88		mhFlagAck = 1 << 1
89	)
90	
91	// ErrChannelClosed is returned by a write or a close on a channel whose
92	// write side has already been closed.
93	var ErrChannelClosed = errors.New("codec: channel closed")
94	
95	// MuxConfig configures a Mux.
96	type MuxConfig struct {
97		// Channels is the number of logical channels the session carries,
98		// numbered 0..Channels-1. It must be positive.
99		Channels int
100	
101		// Window is the per-channel in-flight quota in frames, enforced
102		// independently for every channel (and the receive-side reach used
103		// to place inbound sequences). It must be positive.
104		Window int
105	
106		// StateDir holds the per-channel checkpoint files and the shared
107		// replay journal used to resume the write side after a restart. It
108		// is created if missing.
109		StateDir string
110	}

112	// ChannelFrame is one caller-visible multiplexed frame. Channel names
113	// the channel it was written to.
114	type ChannelFrame struct {
115		Channel uint16
116		Flags   uint16
117		Kind    uint8
118		Payload []byte
119	}
120	
121	// queuedFrame is one accepted send-side frame waiting for a
122	// transmission opportunity or an acknowledgement.
123	type queuedFrame struct {
124		channel uint16
125		seq     uint32
126		flags   uint16
127		kind    uint8
128		payload []byte
129		fin     bool
130	}

132	// sendChannel is one direction of one channel on the send side.
133	type sendChannel struct {
134		// next is the next sequence a write gets; acked is the cumulative
135		// "next expected" position confirmed by the peer. In-flight quota is
136		// exactly next-acked because rejected frames consume no sequence.
137		next   uint32
138		acked  uint32
139		open   bool // opened by a first write or close
140		closed bool // write side closed (the FIN may still be queued)
141	}
142	
143	// inboundFrame is a parked receive-side frame; fin markers carry no
144	// caller frame.
145	type inboundFrame struct {
146		cf  ChannelFrame
147		fin bool
148	}
149	
150	// muxSeq identifies a frame within one channel.
151	type muxSeq struct {
152		ch  uint16
153		seq uint32
154	}

156	// Mux is a multiplexing layer wrapping one ReliableSession. Create it
157	// with NewMux; the wrapped session must not be used directly while the
158	// Mux owns it.
159	type Mux struct {
160		rel *ReliableSession
161		cfg MuxConfig
162	
163		mu    sync.Mutex
164		queue []*queuedFrame // accepted, unacknowledged frames, arrival order
165		sc    []sendChannel
166		// rr is the round-robin cursor: the channel at which the next Flush
167		// starts handing out opportunities.
168		rr  int
169		log *muxLog
170	
171		rmu sync.Mutex
172		// bases is the per-channel next-due receive sequence; finEOF marks
173		// channels whose FIN already reached the reader. seen remembers the
174		// first copy of every sequence inside the duplicate span (the
175		// window width behind the base) so a retransmitted frame that
176		// conflicts with its first arrival is refused even after that
177		// sequence was delivered and left held.
178		bases  []uint32
179		seen   map[muxSeq]inboundFrame
180		held   map[muxSeq]inboundFrame
181		finEOF []bool
182		rerr   error
183	
184		// standCh coalesces standalone ack send requests; capacity Channels
185		// keeps one pending position per channel because acks are cumulative.
186		standCh chan standAck
187		stopCh  chan struct{}
188		doneCh  chan struct{}
189	}

191	// standAck is one standalone channel acknowledgement handed to the
192	// background sender.
193	type standAck struct {
194		ch   uint16
195		next uint32
196	}

198	// NewMux wraps rel in a multiplexing session. Write state in
199	// cfg.StateDir is consulted when present: a fresh directory starts
200	// every channel at sequence 0, while a directory left by a crashed or
201	// restarted process resumes from the earliest confirmed per-channel
202	// positions held by its checkpoints and journal.
203	//
204	// A truncated journal or a flipped bit in a complete record fails
205	// recovery with ErrChecksum rather than replaying unverified frames.
206	func NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error) {
207		if cfg.Channels <= 0 {
208			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux channel count must be positive")
209		}
210		if cfg.Window <= 0 {
211			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux window must be positive")
212		}
213		if cfg.StateDir == "" {
214			return nil, errors.New("codec: mux session requires a state directory")
215		}
216		if err := os.MkdirAll(cfg.StateDir, 0o755); err != nil {
217			return nil, err
218		}
219	
220		m := &Mux{
221			rel:     rel,
222			cfg:     cfg,
223			sc:      make([]sendChannel, cfg.Channels),
224			bases:   make([]uint32, cfg.Channels),
225			seen:    make(map[muxSeq]inboundFrame),
226			held:    make(map[muxSeq]inboundFrame),
227			finEOF:  make([]bool, cfg.Channels),
228			standCh: make(chan standAck, cfg.Channels),
229			stopCh:  make(chan struct{}),
230			doneCh:  make(chan struct{}),
231		}
232	
233		// Load the strict shared journal first, then reconcile per-channel
234		// positions against the checkpoints.
235		var err error
236		m.log, err = openMuxLog(cfg.StateDir)
237		if err != nil {
238			return nil, err
239		}
240	
241		// Per-channel bookkeeping derived strictly from the journal: lowest
242		// and one-past-highest sequence, whether a FIN was seen, and strict
243		// contiguity (a gap or a duplicate would mean a skipped or doubled
244		// frame, which recovery must never silently replay).
245		type span struct {
246			min, max uint32
247			have     bool
248			fin      bool
249		}
250		spans := make([]span, cfg.Channels)
251		for _, rec := range m.log.recs {
252			if int(rec.ch) >= cfg.Channels {
253				return nil, fmt.Errorf("codec: mux journal carries channel %d beyond %d: %w",
254					rec.ch, cfg.Channels-1, ErrChecksum)
255			}
256			sp := &spans[rec.ch]
257			if sp.have {
258				if rec.seq != sp.max+1 {
259					return nil, fmt.Errorf(
260						"codec: mux journal ch %d not contiguous (seq %d after %d): %w",
261						rec.ch, rec.seq, sp.max, ErrChecksum)
262				}
263				if sp.fin {
264					return nil, fmt.Errorf(
265						"codec: mux journal ch %d has frame seq %d after FIN: %w",
266						rec.ch, rec.seq, ErrChecksum)
267				}
268			}
269			if !sp.have {
270				sp.min, sp.have = rec.seq, true
271			}
272			sp.max = rec.seq
273			if rec.fin {
274				sp.fin = true
275			}
276		}
277	
278		for ch := 0; ch < cfg.Channels; ch++ {
279			cpAck, err := loadMuxCheckpoint(cfg.StateDir, uint16(ch))
280			if err != nil {
281				return nil, err
282			}
283			c := &m.sc[ch]
284			sp := spans[ch]
285			switch {
286			case !sp.have:
287				// Nothing left to replay: resume numbering at the confirmed
288				// position; earlier sequences already reached the peer.
289				c.acked, c.next = cpAck, cpAck
290			case cpAck >= sp.max+1:
291				// Checkpoint at/beyond the journal tail.
292				c.acked, c.next = cpAck, cpAck
293			default:
294				// The journal reaches further back than the checkpoint (a
295				// crash between checkpoint and prefix). Resume at the
296				// EARLIER position: the overlap is resent and the receiver
297				// deduplicates it; starting later would skip an
298				// unacknowledged frame.
299				c.acked, c.next = sp.min, sp.max+1
300			}
301			if sp.have {
302				c.open = true
303				c.closed = sp.fin
304			}
305		}
306	
307		// The send queue is the journal in arrival order, minus frames
308		// already at/behind their channel's resumed position; it feeds
309		// round-robin Flush and bounds in-flight accounting.
310		m.queue = make([]*queuedFrame, 0, len(m.log.recs))
311		for i := range m.log.recs {
312			rec := m.log.recs[i]
313			if rec.seq < m.sc[rec.ch].acked {
314				continue
315			}
316			qf := rec.frame()
317			m.queue = append(m.queue, &qf)
318		}
319	
320		go m.pumpAck()
321		return m, nil
322	}
323	
324	// WriteFrame enqueues f on channel f.Channel and assigns it that
325	// channel's next sequence; nothing reaches the wire before Flush.
326	//
327	// It returns ErrTooLarge for a payload larger than MuxMaxPayload, the
328	// established checksum value for a channel number outside the session,
329	// ErrWindowFull when the channel already holds Window unacknowledged
330	// frames, and ErrChannelClosed when the channel's write side has been
331	// closed. A rejected frame is neither queued nor journaled and consumes
332	// no sequence.
333	func (m *Mux) WriteFrame(f ChannelFrame) error {
334		if len(f.Payload) > MuxMaxPayload {
335			return ErrTooLarge
336		}
337		if int(f.Channel) >= m.cfg.Channels {
338			return fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d out of range [0,%d): %w",
339				f.Channel, m.cfg.Channels, ErrChecksum)
340		}
341	
342		m.mu.Lock()
343		defer m.mu.Unlock()
344	
345		c := &m.sc[f.Channel]
346		if c.closed {
347			return ErrChannelClosed
348		}
349		if c.next-c.acked >= uint32(m.cfg.Window) {
350			return ErrWindowFull
351		}
352	
353		qf := queuedFrame{
354			channel: f.Channel,
355			seq:     c.next,
356			flags:   f.Flags,
357			kind:    f.Kind,
358			payload: append([]byte(nil), f.Payload...),
359		}
360		if err := m.log.append(qf); err != nil {
361			return err
362		}
363		c.open = true
364		c.next++
365		m.queue = append(m.queue, &qf)
366		return nil
367	}
368	
369	// CloseChannel closes the write side of ch. The FIN is itself a framed
370	// sequence entry: it consumes one in-flight slot, so a full quota makes
371	// CloseChannel return ErrWindowFull and the caller retries after acks
372	// arrive. Closing a channel that was never written opens it first, so an
373	// unused channel still delivers a clean io.EOF to the peer. Closing (or
374	// writing to) an already closed channel returns ErrChannelClosed.
375	func (m *Mux) CloseChannel(ch uint16) error {
376		if int(ch) >= m.cfg.Channels {
377			return fmt.Errorf("codec: mux channel %d out of range [0,%d): %w",
378				ch, m.cfg.Channels, ErrChecksum)
379		}
380	
381		m.mu.Lock()
382		defer m.mu.Unlock()
383	
384		c := &m.sc[ch]
385		if c.closed {
386			return ErrChannelClosed
387		}
388		if c.next-c.acked >= uint32(m.cfg.Window) {
389			return ErrWindowFull
390		}
391	
392		qf := queuedFrame{channel: ch, seq: c.next, fin: true}
393		if err := m.log.append(qf); err != nil {
394			return err
395		}
396		c.open = true
397		c.closed = true
398		c.next++
399		m.queue = append(m.queue, &qf)
400		return nil
401	}
402	
403	// Flush sends every queued frame with transmission opportunities handed
404	// out round-robin across channels: starting where the previous Flush
405	// stopped, each pass takes at most one queued frame per channel, so a
406	// continuously busy channel can never starve the others and frames
407	// never overtake an earlier frame of their own channel. Every data
408	// frame piggybacks the sender's current receive position for its
409	// channel; standalone acks for every channel follow the run.
410	//
411	// After a restart the queue was reloaded from the journal, so Flush is
412	// also the retransmit operation; the receiver deduplicates overlaps.
413	func (m *Mux) Flush() error {
414		// Snapshot receive positions BEFORE taking the send lock: the read
415		// path takes mu while applying acks (rmu-then-mu order), so mu must
416		// never be held while taking rmu.
417		m.rmu.Lock()
418		acks := make([]uint32, m.cfg.Channels)
419		copy(acks, m.bases)
420		m.rmu.Unlock()
421	
422		m.mu.Lock()
423		out, cursor := m.buildFlushLocked(acks)
424		m.mu.Unlock()
425	
426		for i := range out {
427			// The lower session's own window can fill (a restart backlog
428			// wider than one window, or a slow peer). That is backpressure,
429			// not a protocol error: stop enqueueing there, flush the frames
430			// already accepted and leave the rest queued for the next Flush;
431			// the receiver deduplicates the overlap.
432			if err := m.rel.WriteFrame(out[i]); errors.Is(err, ErrWindowFull) {
433				break
434			} else if err != nil {
435				return err
436			}
437		}
438		if err := m.rel.Flush(); err != nil {
439			return err
440		}
441	
442		// The run is on the wire (or durably queued by the lower layer);
443		// advance the round-robin cursor only now so a failed Flush retries
444		// from the same channel.
445		m.mu.Lock()
446		m.rr = cursor
447		m.mu.Unlock()
448		return nil
449	}
450	
451	// buildFlushLocked returns the data frames of one Flush in wire order
452	// and the cursor the next Flush starts at. It never mutates the queue.
453	// The caller holds mu.
454	func (m *Mux) buildFlushLocked(acks []uint32) ([]ReliableFrame, int) {
455		// Entries of one channel are always in ascending seq order (append
456		// order at write time, journal order after a restart); pending just
457		// tracks which have been taken during this Flush.
458		pending := make([]*queuedFrame, len(m.queue))
459		copy(pending, m.queue)
460	
461		out := make([]ReliableFrame, 0, len(pending))
462		cursor := m.rr
463		for len(pending) > 0 {
464			startCh := cursor
465			taken := false
466			for step := 0; step < m.cfg.Channels; step++ {
467				ch := uint16((startCh + step) % m.cfg.Channels)
468				idx := -1
469				for i, qf := range pending {
470					if qf.channel == ch {
471						idx = i
472						break
473					}
474				}
475				if idx < 0 {
476					continue
477				}
478				qf := pending[idx]
479				pending = append(pending[:idx], pending[idx+1:]...)
480				flag := uint8(0)
481				if qf.fin {
482					flag = mhFlagFin
483				}
484				out = append(out, ReliableFrame{
485					Flags:   qf.flags,
486					Kind:    qf.kind,
487					Payload: encodeMuxHeader(qf.channel, qf.seq, flag, acks[qf.channel], qf.payload),
488				})
489				taken = true
490				cursor = int(ch) + 1 // next pass starts after the served channel
491			}
492			if !taken {
493				break
494			}
495		}
496		if cursor >= m.cfg.Channels {
497			cursor = 0
498		}
499		return out, cursor
500	}
501	
502	// ReadFrame returns the next deliverable frame across all channels.
503	// Channels are scanned independently: a channel parked waiting for a
504	// gap is skipped, so it never stalls another channel. Within a channel
505	// frames arrive in write order exactly once; out-of-order frames are
506	// parked until their gap closes.
507	//
508	// When a channel's FIN is reached - after every earlier frame of that
509	// channel was delivered - the call returns io.EOF together with a
510	// ChannelFrame whose Channel names the closed channel; reads on other
511	// channels continue unaffected.
512	//
513	// The following are refused with the established ErrChecksum and stop
514	// delivery stickily at the current positions: a channel number outside
515	// the session's reach, a residual frame older than one channel-window,
516	// a frame more than one channel-window ahead, an acknowledgement past
517	// the send frontier, a same-sequence retransmission with different
518	// content, an unknown flag, an ack frame carrying payload, and a
519	// damaged mux header. Reliable-layer results (the transport's io.EOF,
520	// ErrShortFrame, outer checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass
521	// through unchanged, and complete frames already buffered are delivered
522	// before a terminal lower-layer result is surfaced.
523	func (m *Mux) ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error) {
524		for {
525			m.rmu.Lock()
526			if m.rerr != nil {
527				err := m.rerr
528				m.rmu.Unlock()
529				return ChannelFrame{}, err
530			}
531			if cf, eof, ok := m.nextDeliverableLocked(); ok {
532				m.rmu.Unlock()
533				if eof {
534					return cf, io.EOF
535				}
536				return cf, nil
537			}
538			m.rmu.Unlock()
539	
540			// Block in the reliable reader WITHOUT holding rmu, exactly like
541			// the layer below: sends and ack processing must keep moving
542			// while this waits for bytes.
543			outer, rerr := m.rel.ReadFrame()
544	
545			m.rmu.Lock()
546			if m.rerr != nil {
547				err := m.rerr
548				m.rmu.Unlock()
549				return ChannelFrame{}, err
550			}
551			if rerr != nil {
552				// The lower layer hands over its terminal result together
553				// with any bytes that arrived in the same read; complete
554				// frames already parsed below are parked in held. Deliver
555				// every buffered frame across all channels first, and only
556				// surface the terminal result once the buffer is drained;
557				// the result is sticky and returns again on later calls.
558				if cf, eof, ok := m.nextDeliverableLocked(); ok {
559					m.rmu.Unlock()
560					if eof {
561						return cf, io.EOF
562					}
563					return cf, nil
564				}
565				return m.failReadLocked(rerr)
566			}
567	
568			ch, seq, flag, ack, payload, err := decodeMuxHeader(outer.Payload)
569			if err != nil {
570				return m.failReadLocked(err)
571			}
572			if int(ch) >= m.cfg.Channels {
573				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
574					"codec: mux channel %d out of range [0,%d): %w",
575					ch, m.cfg.Channels, ErrChecksum))
576			}
577			if flag&^uint8(mhFlagFin|mhFlagAck) != 0 {
578				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
579					"codec: mux ch %d seq %d unknown flags %#x: %w",
580					ch, seq, flag, ErrChecksum))
581			}
582			isAck := flag&mhFlagAck != 0
583			isFin := flag&mhFlagFin != 0
584			if isAck && (isFin || seq != 0 || len(payload) != 0) {
585				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
586					"codec: mux ch %d malformed ack frame (fin=%v seq=%d payload=%d): %w",
587					ch, isFin, seq, len(payload), ErrChecksum))
588			}
589			if isFin && len(payload) != 0 {
590				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
591					"codec: mux ch %d FIN seq %d carries %d payload bytes: %w",
592					ch, seq, len(payload), ErrChecksum))
593			}
594	
595			// Every inbound message states a cumulative position for its
596			// channel; one past anything this side ever sent is impossible
597			// in a well-behaved stream and is refused before anything is
598			// parked or delivered.
599			m.mu.Lock()
600			overFrontier := ack > m.sc[ch].next
601			frontier := m.sc[ch].next
602			m.mu.Unlock()
603			if overFrontier {
604				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
605					"codec: mux ch %d ack %d past send frontier %d: %w",
606					ch, ack, frontier, ErrChecksum))
607			}
608			m.applyAck(ch, ack)
609	
610			if isAck {
611				m.rmu.Unlock()
612				continue
613			}
614	
615			cf := ChannelFrame{Channel: ch, Flags: outer.Flags, Kind: outer.Kind, Payload: payload}
616			fr := inboundFrame{cf: cf, fin: isFin}
617			key := muxSeq{ch: ch, seq: seq}
618			base := m.bases[ch]
619			switch classify(seq, base, m.cfg.Window) {
620			case seqInWindow:
621				if prev, dup := m.held[key]; dup {
622					// A retransmission of a parked frame must describe the
623					// same frame. A same-sequence conflict is refused
624					// instead of guessed, and delivery stops here.
625					if !sameInbound(prev, fr) {
626						return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
627							"codec: mux ch %d seq %d retransmission conflicts: %w",
628							ch, seq, ErrChecksum))
629					}
630				} else if prev, seen := m.seen[key]; seen {
631					// Already delivered once: any conflicting second
632					// declaration of the same sequence is a protocol error.
633					if !sameInbound(prev, fr) {
634						return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
635							"codec: mux ch %d seq %d duplicate conflicts with delivered frame: %w",
636							ch, seq, ErrChecksum))
637					}
638				} else {
639					m.held[key] = fr
640				}
641				// Restate the channel's cumulative position either way so a
642				// lost acknowledgement does not make the peer resend
643				// forever.
644				m.signalAckLocked(ch)
645				m.rmu.Unlock()

686	func (m *Mux) nextDeliverableLocked() (cf ChannelFrame, eof bool, ok bool) {
687		for ch := 0; ch < m.cfg.Channels; ch++ {
688			if m.finEOF[ch] {

691			key := muxSeq{ch: uint16(ch), seq: m.bases[ch]}

813	// encodeMuxHeader serializes one mux message into reliable payload
814	// bytes.
815	func encodeMuxHeader(ch uint16, seq uint32, flags uint8, ack uint32, payload []byte) []byte {
816		out := make([]byte, MuxHeaderSize+len(payload))
817		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[mhChanOff:mhSeqOff], ch)
818		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhSeqOff:mhFlagOff], seq)
819		out[mhFlagOff] = flags
820		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhAckOff:mhCRCOff], ack)
821		copy(out[mhBodyOff:], payload)
822		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
823		h.Write(out[:mhCRCOff])
824		h.Write(out[mhBodyOff:])
825		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhCRCOff:mhBodyOff], h.Sum32())
